title: Bhartṛprapañca's commentary on the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (lost)
summary: A pre-Śaṅkara commentary teaching that Brahman is both one and many and that liberation needs knowledge combined with works; known only from reports and refutations in Śaṅkara's Bṛhadāraṇyaka commentary, Sureśvara's Vārttika and Ānandagiri's glosses.

attribution.tradition: Bhartṛprapañca (identified by Ānandagiri as the opponent in Śaṅkara's commentary)

scholarly.text: before Śaṅkara (c. 6th–7th c. CE or earlier)

notes: All knowledge of this work comes from opponents (reported_by_opponent). A commentary on the Kaṭha Upaniṣad is also reported (low confidence).

title: Brahmasūtrabhāṣya of Bhāskara (Bhāskarabhāṣya)
summary: Bhāskara's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras: Brahman really transforms into the world through its power; souls are parts of Brahman distinguished by real adjuncts (aupādhika bhedābheda); liberation comes after death through knowledge combined with lifelong ritual duty; it attacks Śaṅkara's doctrine of māyā as Mahāyāna Buddhist in origin.

structure.description: four adhyāyas, each of four pādas, following the sūtras

scholarly.text: c. 8th–9th c. CE (after Śaṅkara, before Vācaspati who answers him)

title: Bhāskara's commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā
summary: A Gītā commentary ascribed to Bhāskara, reported to survive only in part, arguing the combination of knowledge and action.
notes: Existence and extent to be confirmed in Phase C.

title: Yādavaprakāśa's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras (lost)
summary: A lost commentary teaching natural (svābhāvika) difference-and-non-difference: Brahman itself transforms into Īśvara, souls and matter. Known from Rāmānuja's Vedārthasaṅgraha and Śrībhāṣya and later Śrīvaiṣṇava refutations.

title: Yatidharmasamuccaya
summary: A digest of the rules of Brahmanical renunciation (the renouncer's staff, dress, begging, conduct and daily routine), attributed to Yādavaprakāśa; edited and translated by P. Olivelle.

title: Vaijayantī (lexicon)
summary: A Sanskrit lexicon (kośa) attributed to Yādavaprakāśa.

title: Vijñānāmṛtabhāṣya
summary: Vijñānabhikṣu's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras, presenting a Vedānta of non-separation (avibhāga) — a form of difference-and-non-difference — in which Sāṃkhya and Yoga are integrated and Śaṅkara's māyāvāda is rejected.

title: Vedāntapārijātasaurabha
summary: Nimbārka's brief commentary on the Brahma Sūtras establishing natural difference-and-non-difference: souls and world are Brahman's powers, different and non-different from him like sun and rays or snake and coils.
notes: Translated by Roma Bose (1940–43) with Śrīnivāsa's Vedāntakaustubha.

title: Daśaślokī (Siddhāntaratna; Vedāntakāmadhenu)
summary: Nimbārka's ten verses summarising the school: the soul, bondage and release, the three kinds of non-conscious reality, Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā, worship, the reality of all as Brahman's nature, refuge in Kṛṣṇa alone, grace and devotion, and the five things to be known.

title: Śrīkṛṣṇastavarāja
summary: A hymn to Kṛṣṇa attributed to Nimbārka, stating the school's doctrine in devotional form; commented on by Puruṣottamācārya.

title: Vedāntakaustubha
summary: Śrīnivāsa's commentary on Nimbārka's Vedāntapārijātasaurabha, the classical exposition of the school's reading of the Brahma Sūtras.

title: Vedāntakaustubhaprabhā
summary: Keśava Kāśmīrin's sub-commentary on the Vedāntakaustubha, the school's most extensive Brahma Sūtra exposition.

title: Tattvaprakāśikā (Gītā commentary of Keśava Kāśmīrin)
summary: Keśava Kāśmīrin's commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā from the Dvaitādvaita standpoint.

title: Kramadīpikā
summary: A liturgical manual of Kṛṣṇa-mantra worship attributed to Keśava Kāśmīrin, drawn upon in Gauḍīya ritual (Haribhaktivilāsa).
notes: Attribution and Gauḍīya use to confirm.

title: Vedāntaratnamañjūṣā
summary: Puruṣottamācārya's commentary on the Daśaślokī, systematising the arthapañcaka and the means of attainment.

title: Śrutyantasuradruma
summary: Puruṣottamācārya's commentary on the Śrīkṛṣṇastavarāja.

title: Siddhāntajāhnavī
summary: Devācārya's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras in the Nimbārka school.

title: Yugalaśataka
summary: Śrī Bhaṭṭa's hundred Braj Bhāṣā verses on the love-play of the divine couple (yugala) Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; among the earliest Braj devotional texts.

title: Mahāvāṇī
summary: Harivyāsadeva's Braj Bhāṣā collection of songs on the eternal love-play of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the mood of the sakhīs.

title: Siddhāntaratnāñjali
summary: Harivyāsadeva's Sanskrit commentary on the Daśaślokī.

title: Parapakṣagirivajra
summary: A polemical treatise of the Nimbārka school against Advaita and other rival Vedāntas, attributed to Mādhava Mukunda.

title: Brahmasūtrabhāṣya of Śrīkaṇṭha (Śrīkaṇṭhabhāṣya)
summary: Śrīkaṇṭha Śivācārya's Śaiva commentary on the Brahma Sūtras: Brahman is Śiva endowed with cit-śakti, material and efficient cause; souls and world are his body; the dahara (small space in the heart) is Śiva; Veda and Śaiva Āgama are equal in authority; the liberated attain equality with Śiva.

title: Śivārkamaṇidīpikā
summary: Appayya Dīkṣita's extensive commentary on Śrīkaṇṭha's Brahmasūtrabhāṣya, reviving the Śaiva Vedānta in the 16th century.

title: Śivādvaitanirṇaya
summary: Appayya Dīkṣita's short treatise arguing that Śrīkaṇṭha's qualified non-dualism ultimately intends pure non-dualism (Advaita).

title: Ratnatrayaparīkṣā
summary: Appayya Dīkṣita's short work on the 'three jewels' — Śiva, his Śakti and Viṣṇu (as Śiva's śakti) — from a Śaiva standpoint.

title: Śivatattvaviveka
summary: Appayya Dīkṣita's defence of Śiva's supremacy on scriptural grounds.

title: Śrīkarabhāṣya
summary: Śrīpati Paṇḍita's Vīraśaiva commentary on the Brahma Sūtras, naming the doctrine Śakti-viśiṣṭādvaita: the non-duality of Śiva (liṅga) and the soul (aṅga), both qualified by Śakti, realised as their union (liṅgāṅga-sāmarasya).

scholarly.text: c. 14th c. CE (disputed; some place it earlier)

notes: Contributed by U16 for its philosophy; Vīraśaiva lineage entries are owned by U20.

title: Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi
summary: Śivayogi Śivācārya's Sanskrit exposition of Vīraśaiva doctrine as Reṇukācārya's instruction to Agastya, expanding the six stages (ṣaṭsthala) into 101 stations (sthala) and teaching the qualified non-duality of Śiva and soul through Śakti.
notes: Owned by U20; U16 contributes the Śakti-viśiṣṭādvaita reading.

title: Aṇubhāṣya (Brahmasūtrāṇubhāṣya)
summary: Vallabha's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras establishing Śuddhādvaita: Brahman is the material and efficient cause and becomes the world without change (avikṛta-pariṇāma); it is the locus of contradictory attributes. Vallabha's own text breaks off in the third adhyāya and was completed by his son Viṭṭhalanātha.
notes: The point at which Vallabha's portion ends (c. BS 3.2.33) is commonly stated; verify.

title: Tattvārthadīpanibandha (with Vallabha's Prakāśa)
summary: Vallabha's verse summa with his own prose commentary (Prakāśa), in three parts: Śāstrārtha-prakaraṇa (the doctrine, on the basis of the Gītā), Sarvanirṇaya-prakaraṇa (the pramāṇas, the goal, the means) and Bhāgavatārtha-prakaraṇa (the meaning of the Bhāgavata, canto by canto).

title: Subodhinī (Vallabha's commentary on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
summary: Vallabha's commentary on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, extant for cantos 1–3, much of 10 and part of 11; reads the tenth canto as 'nirodha' — the Lord's play drawing souls away from the world into himself — and the gopīs' love as the model of grace-devotion.

title: Ṣoḍaśagrantha (the sixteen short works of Vallabha)
summary: Sixteen brief verse treatises that give the Puṣṭimārga's practical teaching on grace, service, refuge, the kinds of souls, the stages of devotion, renunciation and absorption.

title: Yamunāṣṭaka
summary: Eight verses praising the Yamunā as Kṛṣṇa's beloved and the giver of grace-devotion.

title: Bālabodha
summary: On the four aims of life as taught in different paths, and the devotee's aim.

title: Siddhāntamuktāvalī
summary: On the nature of service (sevā) and the three forms of the one reality, illustrated by the Gaṅgā seen as water, holy river and goddess.

title: Puṣṭipravāhamaryādābheda
summary: On the differences between the three kinds of souls and paths: grace (puṣṭi), rule (maryādā) and worldly stream (pravāha).

title: Siddhāntarahasya
summary: Records the Lord's midnight instruction at Gokul on the brahmasambandha initiation, which removes the five kinds of faults, and the rule of using only what has been offered.

title: Navaratna
summary: Nine verses teaching that those who have offered themselves should never be anxious, for all happens by the Lord's will.

title: Antaḥkaraṇaprabodha
summary: Vallabha's admonition to his own mind to rely on the Lord and obey his command.

title: Vivekadhairyāśraya
summary: On discrimination (viveka), fortitude (dhairya) and taking refuge (āśraya) in the Lord.

title: Kṛṣṇāśraya
summary: In the Kali age, when all paths are ruined, Kṛṣṇa alone is the refuge (refrain: kṛṣṇa eva gatir mama).

title: Catuḥślokī (of Vallabha)
summary: Four verses redefining the four aims of life for the devotee: dharma is always serving the Lord of Vraja with one's whole being.

title: Bhaktivardhinī
summary: On the growth of devotion from its seed through love (prema/sneha) and attachment (āsakti) to consuming absorption (vyasana).

title: Jalabheda
summary: Compares the kinds of speakers of the Lord's glories to kinds of water.

title: Pañcapadyāni
summary: Five verses on the kinds of listeners to the Lord's stories.

title: Sannyāsanirṇaya
summary: On renunciation in the path of devotion, distinguishing it from the renunciation of the knowledge path.

title: Nirodhalakṣaṇa
summary: On nirodha: absorption in the Lord through forgetting the world, and love in separation.

title: Sevāphala
summary: On the fruits of service (supernatural capacity, union, a body fit for service) and its obstacles (agitation, hindrance, enjoyment).

title: Madhurāṣṭaka
summary: Eight verses declaring that everything of Kṛṣṇa, the lord of sweetness, is sweet (adharaṃ madhuraṃ …).

title: Patrāvalambana
summary: A short polemical text Vallabha is said to have posted at the Viśvanātha temple in Kāśī, challenging rival Vedāntins on the unity of the Vedic karma and jñāna sections under Brahmavāda.

title: Puruṣottamasahasranāma
summary: A thousand names of Kṛṣṇa compiled by Vallabha from the Bhāgavata, arranged by its narrative.

title: Vidvanmaṇḍana
summary: Viṭṭhalanātha's polemical defence of Śuddhādvaita against Advaita (with Puruṣottama's commentary Suvarṇasūtra).

title: Śṛṅgārarasamaṇḍana
summary: Viṭṭhalanātha's Sanskrit work on the erotic devotional mood (śṛṅgāra) toward Kṛṣṇa, including Rādhā (Svāminī).

title: Śuddhādvaitamārtaṇḍa
summary: A later Sanskrit manual of Śuddhādvaita doctrine attributed to Giridhara Gosvāmī.

title: Prameyaratnārṇava
summary: A later Sanskrit manual of Puṣṭimārga doctrine attributed to Bālakṛṣṇa Bhaṭṭa.

title: Prasthānaratnākara
summary: Puruṣottama's treatise on the sources of knowledge (prasthāna) in Śuddhādvaita.

title: Bhāṣyaprakāśa
summary: Puruṣottama's commentary on the Aṇubhāṣya.

title: Caurāsī Vaiṣṇavan kī Vārtā
summary: Braj Bhāṣā prose accounts of eighty-four disciples of Vallabha (including Sūrdās, Kumbhandās, Paramānanddās and Kṛṣṇadās), attributed to Gokulnāth, with Harirāy's commentary Bhāvaprakāś.

scholarly.text: 17th c. CE in its present form

title: Do Sau Bāvan Vaiṣṇavan kī Vārtā
summary: Accounts of 252 disciples of Viṭṭhalanātha, including the other four aṣṭachāp poets, attributed to Gokulnāth/Harirāy.

title: Sūrsāgar
summary: The 'ocean of Sūr': Braj Bhāṣā songs on Kṛṣṇa's childhood, the gopīs' love and their separation (the bhramargīt), attributed to Sūrdās. The Puṣṭimārga counts Sūrdās its foremost aṣṭachāp poet.

attribution.scholarly: only a few hundred poems are attested in 16th-c. manuscripts (e.g. the Fatehpur manuscript of 1582); the sectarian affiliation is not visible in the earliest manuscripts

notes: Registry id; primary owner U26/U27. U16 contributes the Puṣṭimārga account.

title: Rāspañcādhyāyī (of Nanddās)
summary: Nanddās's Braj Bhāṣā rendering of the five chapters of the rāsa dance (BhP 10.29–33).

title: Śikṣāṣṭaka
summary: Eight verses ascribed to Caitanya, his only writing: the glory of congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa's name, the name's full potency, the humility with which to chant, the prayer for causeless devotion, and the longing of separation.

attribution.tradition: Caitanya's own verses, preserved by Rūpa (Padyāvalī) and recited by Caitanya at the end of his life (CC 3.20)
attribution.scholarly: the verses appear individually in Rūpa's Padyāvalī; their collection as an eight-verse set is attested in the Caitanya Caritāmṛta

title: Bhaktirasāmṛtasindhu
summary: Rūpa Gosvāmī's treatise on devotion as rasa, in four divisions (east, south, west, north) subdivided into waves (laharī): (1) devotion in general, sādhana-, bhāva- and prema-bhakti, vaidhī and rāgānugā practice and the 64 limbs; (2) the components of rasa (vibhāva, anubhāva, sāttvika, vyabhicārin, sthāyin); (3) the five primary devotional rasas; (4) the seven secondary rasas and their incompatibilities.

scholarly.text: completed 1541 CE (Śaka 1463, per the final verse)

title: Ujjvalanīlamaṇi
summary: Rūpa Gosvāmī's supplement on the 'brilliant' (ujjvala) or amorous rasa (madhura) toward Kṛṣṇa: the hero and heroines, Rādhā and the gopīs, their groups and messengers, the stages of love from prema to mahābhāva, and love in union and separation; holds paramour love in Vraja to be the highest.

title: Laghubhāgavatāmṛta
summary: Rūpa's theology of the Lord's forms: Kṛṣṇa as the original form (svayaṃ-rūpa), his identical expansions (tad-ekātma-rūpa: vilāsa and svāṃśa) and empowered descents (āveśa); the classes of avatāras; and (second part) the devotees in ascending order.

title: Bṛhadbhāgavatāmṛta
summary: Sanātana Gosvāmī's narrative theology with his own commentary Digdarśinī: part 1, Nārada's search for the greatest recipient of Kṛṣṇa's grace, rising to the gopīs; part 2, the cowherd Gopakumāra's journey through the worlds to Goloka.

structure.description: two parts, each of seven chapters

title: Haribhaktivilāsa
summary: The Gauḍīya code of Vaiṣṇava ritual and conduct in twenty 'vilāsas': the guru and disciple and their testing, initiation, daily purity and worship, deity worship with nyāsa and bhūta-śuddhi, the name and offences, the Ekādaśī fast and festivals, temple construction and consecration.

attribution.tradition: compiled by Gopāla Bhaṭṭa (named in the text) with Sanātana's commentary Digdarśinī; some accounts credit Sanātana with the compilation itself

title: Ṣaṭ Sandarbha (Bhāgavata Sandarbha)
summary: Jīva Gosvāmī's six 'compositions' systematising Gauḍīya theology from the Bhāgavata: four on the relation (sambandha: Tattva, Bhagavat, Paramātma, Kṛṣṇa), one on the means (abhidheya: Bhakti) and one on the goal (prayojana: Prīti). Jīva states that he rearranged and completed a draft by a southern Bhaṭṭa (Gopāla Bhaṭṭa), friend of Rūpa and Sanātana.

title: Tattvasandarbha
summary: On the means of knowledge: revelation (śabda) is supreme; among scriptures the Purāṇas, and among them the Bhāgavata, are decisive; the Bhāgavata is the natural commentary on the Brahma Sūtras.

title: Bhagavatsandarbha
summary: On Bhagavān: the personal Lord with his inherent powers is the full manifestation of the non-dual reality, of which impersonal Brahman is an incomplete manifestation.

title: Paramātmasandarbha
summary: On the Paramātman, the souls as the Lord's marginal power, the world as a real transformation of his external power, and the refutation of vivarta.

title: Kṛṣṇasandarbha
summary: On Kṛṣṇa as the Lord himself (BhP 1.3.28 as the governing statement), his eternal abodes and associates, and Rādhā's supremacy among his consorts.

title: Bhaktisandarbha
summary: On devotion as the one means: its kinds, the guru, the limbs of practice, the primacy of congregational chanting of the name in the Kali age, and the offences to be avoided.

title: Prītisandarbha
summary: On love (prīti/prema) as the supreme human goal, beyond liberation, its nature, grades and highest form in the gopīs and Rādhā.

title: Sarvasaṃvādinī
summary: Jīva's own supplementary commentary on the first four Sandarbhas, where the relation of the Lord and his powers is named inconceivable difference-and-non-difference (acintya-bhedābheda).

title: Kramasandarbha
summary: Jīva's running commentary on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, counted as the seventh Sandarbha.

title: Caitanya Caritāmṛta
summary: Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja's Bengali verse biography and theology of Caitanya, interspersed with Sanskrit verses, in three parts: Ādi (17 chapters), Madhya (25) and Antya (20). It sets out who Caitanya is (Kṛṣṇa with Rādhā's mood), his teachings to Rūpa, Sanātana, Rāmānanda, Sārvabhauma and Prakāśānanda, and his last years of divine madness at Purī.

structure.description: 3 līlās: Ādi 17, Madhya 25, Antya 20 chapters (cited here as 1.x.y, 2.x.y, 3.x.y)

scholarly.text: completed c. 1612–1615 CE (one colophon reading gives 1615; an alternative reading 1581)

title: Caitanya Bhāgavata
summary: Vṛndāvana Dāsa's Bengali biography of Caitanya (originally titled Caitanya Maṅgala), rich on the Navadvīpa period, the nocturnal kīrtanas and Nityānanda; in three khaṇḍas (Ādi, Madhya, Antya).

title: Govinda-bhāṣya
summary: Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa's commentary on the Brahma Sūtras for the Gauḍīya school, reading them as teaching Kṛṣṇa (Govinda) as Brahman, the reality of the world and souls, and devotion as the means; it uses Madhva's category of viśeṣa to explain the unity of the Lord and his attributes.

attribution.tradition: written at Galta (Jaipur) at Govindadeva's command in a dream, to establish the Gauḍīyas' own Brahma Sūtra commentary
attribution.scholarly: composed in the context of the early-18th-c. Jaipur examinations of Gauḍīya orthodoxy

title: Prameyaratnāvalī
summary: Baladeva's short manual of nine doctrinal tenets (prameya) with the guru-paramparā traced through Madhva.

title: Siddhāntaratna (of Baladeva)
summary: Baladeva's companion treatise to the Govinda-bhāṣya on the Lord, his powers and qualities.

title: Gītābhūṣaṇa
summary: Baladeva's commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā.

title: Upadeśāmṛta
summary: Rūpa's eleven verses of practical instruction: control of the six urges, six things that destroy and six that nourish devotion, six loving exchanges among devotees, how to honour three kinds of Vaiṣṇavas, the essence of practice (remembering the name, form and play while living in Vraja under those who love him), and the pre-eminence of Rādhākuṇḍa.

title: Vidagdhamādhava
summary: Rūpa's seven-act Sanskrit drama of Kṛṣṇa's love-play with Rādhā in Vraja (1532/33 CE per the text).

title: Lalitamādhava
summary: Rūpa's ten-act drama of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes in Vraja, Mathurā and Dvārakā, ending in Rādhā's reunion with him (1537 CE per the text).

title: Dānakelikaumudī
summary: Rūpa's one-act play (bhāṇikā) on the toll-tax sport at Govardhana.

title: Padyāvalī
summary: Rūpa's anthology of devotional verses by many poets, including the verses later gathered as Caitanya's Śikṣāṣṭaka.

title: Stavamālā
summary: Rūpa's hymns, compiled by Jīva.

title: Haṃsadūta
summary: Rūpa's messenger poem: Lalitā sends a swan to Kṛṣṇa in Mathurā with Rādhā's message of separation.

title: Uddhavasandeśa
summary: Rūpa's messenger poem: Kṛṣṇa sends Uddhava with a message to the gopīs.

title: Nāṭakacandrikā
summary: Rūpa's treatise on dramaturgy for devotional drama, following Bharata's Nāṭyaśāstra.

title: Gopālacampū
summary: Jīva's prose-and-verse narrative of Kṛṣṇa's Vraja pastimes in two parts, in which the gopīs' love is presented as ultimately svakīyā (culminating in Rādhā's marriage to Kṛṣṇa).

title: Harināmāmṛtavyākaraṇa
summary: Jīva's Sanskrit grammar in which every technical term is replaced by names of Kṛṣṇa, so that learning grammar is remembering the Lord.

title: Durgamasaṅgamanī
summary: Jīva's commentary on the Bhaktirasāmṛtasindhu.

title: Locanarocanī
summary: Jīva's commentary on the Ujjvalanīlamaṇi, containing his svakīyā reading and the verse on having written some things by his own wish and some by others'.

title: Bṛhad-Vaiṣṇavatoṣaṇī
summary: Sanātana's commentary on the tenth canto of the Bhāgavata (abridged by Jīva as the Laghutoṣaṇī).

title: Stavāvalī
summary: Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī's hymns and prayers, including the Manaḥśikṣā, the Vilāpakusumāñjali and the Svaniyamadaśaka.

title: Manaḥśikṣā
summary: Raghunātha Dāsa's twelve verses instructing his own mind in spontaneous devotion to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and warning against desire for prestige and crookedness.

title: Vilāpakusumāñjali
summary: Raghunātha Dāsa's lament of a maidservant (mañjarī) longing for the service of Rādhā; a root text of mañjarī-bhāva.

title: Govindalīlāmṛta
summary: Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja's Sanskrit poem on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa's pastimes through the eight periods of the day (aṣṭakālīya-līlā).

title: Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta
summary: Bilvamaṅgala (Līlāśuka)'s lyrical hymns on Kṛṣṇa's beauty and play; brought from south India by Caitanya (CC 2.9) and commented on by Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja (Sāraṅgaraṅgadā).

title: Brahma Saṃhitā (fifth chapter)
summary: The fifth chapter of a Pāñcarātra-style saṃhitā, Brahmā's hymn to Govinda as the supreme Lord whose form is being, consciousness and bliss, residing in Goloka among his own potencies; tradition says Caitanya found it at the Ādikeśava temple in south India (CC 2.9); commented on by Jīva.

title: Caitanyacandrodaya
summary: Kavikarṇapūra's ten-act Sanskrit drama on Caitanya's life (1572 CE per tradition).

title: Gauragaṇoddeśadīpikā
summary: Kavikarṇapūra's identification of Caitanya's associates with figures of Kṛṣṇa's play (1576 CE), with the guru-paramparā from Madhva.

title: Caitanya Maṅgala (of Locana Dāsa)
summary: Locana Dāsa's Bengali song-biography of Caitanya, based on Murāri Gupta.

title: Caitanya Maṅgala (of Jayānanda)
summary: Jayānanda's Bengali biography of Caitanya, notable for an account of his death.

title: Śrīkṛṣṇacaitanyacaritāmṛtam (Murāri Gupta's kaḍacā)
summary: The earliest Sanskrit biography of Caitanya by his Navadvīpa companion Murāri Gupta.

title: Prema-bhakti-candrikā
summary: Narottama Dāsa's Bengali songs setting out the Gauḍīya path of devotion under the Gosvāmīs' guidance.

title: Bhaktiratnākara
summary: Narahari Cakravartī's 18th-c. Bengali chronicle of the second generation (Śrīnivāsa, Narottama, Śyāmānanda), the transport of the Gosvāmīs' books to Bengal and the Kheturi festival.

title: Satkriyāsāradīpikā
summary: A Vaiṣṇava manual of household sacraments (saṃskāra) attributed to Gopāla Bhaṭṭa.

title: Mādhuryakādambinī
summary: Viśvanātha Cakravartin's treatise elaborating Rūpa's stages from faith to love: the kinds of obstacles (anartha), the unsteady phases of practice, the obstacles to steadiness and the growth of taste, attachment, emotion and love.

title: Rāgavartmacandrikā
summary: Viśvanātha's short treatise on spontaneous devotion (rāgānugā): eager longing (lobha) as its sole qualification and the method of serving in one's practitioner's body and inner perfected body.

title: Sārārthadarśinī
summary: Viśvanātha's commentary on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa.

title: Sārārthavarṣiṇī
summary: Viśvanātha's commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā.

title: Ānandacandrikā
summary: Viśvanātha's commentary on the Ujjvalanīlamaṇi, defending paramour love (parakīyā) as eternal.

title: Kṛṣṇabhāvanāmṛta
summary: Viśvanātha's poem on the eightfold daily pastimes for meditative remembrance.

title: Gopālatāpanī Upaniṣad
summary: A Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad on Kṛṣṇa (Gopāla) as the supreme, his mantra and meditation in Vṛndāvana; commented on by Jīva (Sukhabodhinī) and valued by the Nimbārka school.
notes: Minor Upaniṣad; primary owner U04. Its eighteen-syllable mantra is given only at initiation and is not reproduced here.

title: Kalisantaraṇa Upaniṣad
summary: A short Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad in which Brahmā teaches Nārada that the sixteen names 'hare rāma … hare kṛṣṇa …' destroy the evils of the Kali age and that no better means is found in all the Vedas.
notes: Minor Upaniṣad; primary owner U04 (id by slug rule).

title: Bhāvārthadīpikā
summary: Śrīdhara Svāmin's commentary on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, blending non-dualism with devotion; revered by Caitanya and the Gauḍīyas.

title: Jaiva Dharma
summary: Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's Bengali novel-treatise presenting Gauḍīya doctrine and practice through dialogues (1896).

title: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is
summary: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami's English translation and Gauḍīya commentary on the Gītā (1968; enlarged 1972), the basic text of ISKCON.
